work_completed: Discovered that the previously-applied ~/.config/zed/settings.json context_servers.asfdk-harness.command override had been silently wiped back to `{}` (Zed's Extensions panel 'Configure' button appears to rewrite that block to the extension's bare defaults), and that the timeout recurred after a Zed restart even with the correct override in place.

Noticed a second, unrelated extension ('mcp-server-nextjs') hit the exact same 'Context server request timeout' failure, which ruled out anything specific to our command/path resolution and pointed at either a Zed-side bug or a bug shared by both MCP servers.

Fetched Zed's actual open-source implementation (zed-industries/zed@main: crates/context_server/src/{client.rs,transport/stdio_transport.rs}, crates/util/src/{shell.rs,shell_builder.rs}) and confirmed the stdio framing (raw newline-delimited JSON-RPC, matching the MCP spec), shell-wrapping (non-interactive `sh -c`, no rc-file sourcing), and request/response id matching are all correct — ruling out a Zed-side transport bug.

Empirically replicated Zed's exact spawn invocation (absolute node path + absolute script path, wrapped in `bash -c "..."` exactly as ShellBuilder would construct it) directly in a terminal and confirmed it answers a raw MCP `initialize` handshake instantly — further confirming Zed's side and the direct-path invocation were both fine.

Root-caused the actual bug to this repo's source: src/mcp-server.ts, src/a2a-proxy.ts, src/discovery-hub.ts, and src/mcp-http-server.ts all guarded their main() call with `if (process.argv[1] && import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href)`. This idiom breaks for any symlink-based invocation (exactly how npm/pnpm/yarn wire up package.json#bin, including `npm link`): Node resolves import.meta.url to the realpath but leaves process.argv[1] as the invoked (symlink) path, so the comparison never matches, main() silently never runs, and the process exits cleanly (exit 0) without ever touching stdio — indistinguishable from a hang to a client waiting on a response.

Confirmed this empirically with a disposable symlinked probe script (printed process.argv[1] vs import.meta.url vs pathToFileURL(argv[1]).href before/after symlinking) and by directly invoking `asfdk-harness-mcp` (installed via `npm link`) before the fix, observing zero output / silent exit 0 with no MCP response.

Fixed by adding src/entrypoint.ts exporting isMainModule(moduleUrl), which compares fs.realpathSync() on both sides instead of the raw string/URL comparison, and switched all four affected entry points to use it.

Ran `npm run build`, then `npm link` (explicitly using the same nvm-managed npm that Zed's own process resolves via PATH, confirmed by reading /proc/<zed-pid>/environ) so the `asfdk-harness-mcp` fallback command genuinely resolves and works for Zed's context-server PATH fallback, not just in a shell with different PATH resolution.

Verified the fix end-to-end: piping a raw MCP initialize JSON-RPC request through the symlinked `asfdk-harness-mcp` PATH command (and through a `bash -c` wrapper matching Zed's ShellBuilder output) now returns the correct instant response, where before the fix it silently returned nothing.

Ran the full test suite (`npm run test:unit`): 76 tests, 73 pass, 3 fail. Confirmed via `git stash` that the exact same 3 failures (asfdk package version drift in a wiring test, plus a `before_agent_start` hook-registration assertion in test/extension-load.test.ts) exist identically on the pre-change baseline — not a regression introduced by this fix, and out of scope for this task.

Re-applied the ~/.config/zed/settings.json command override (belt-and-suspenders; no longer strictly required now that the PATH fallback works) and rewrote the zed-extension/README.md Troubleshooting section, and the root README.md local-setup snippet, to lead with the source-level fix and `npm link` as the durable setup path, documenting the Configure-button settings-reset quirk as a known caveat.
Updated docs/active-threads.md THREAD-012 with a session-4 entry superseding the earlier (partially incorrect / incomplete) settings-override-only diagnosis.
Committed src/entrypoint.ts, the four entry-point fixes, and all doc updates to feat/kilo-plugin and pushed to origin (no direct push to main; PR still TBD).
decisions_made: Fix the root cause in TypeScript source (src/entrypoint.ts + 4 call sites) rather than only patching around it in the Zed extension or Zed settings, since the bug affects every symlink-based invocation of these four CLI entry points (npm link, npm/pnpm/yarn global install), not just the Zed dev-extension scenario.

Keep the Zed settings.json command override in place as an optional, explicit, redundant safeguard, but no longer document it as the primary/required fix now that the underlying PATH fallback is fixed and durable.

Did not investigate or attempt to fix the 3 pre-existing, unrelated test failures (asfdk package version assertion, before_agent_start hook registration) since they predate this session's changes (confirmed via git stash comparison) and are out of scope.
decisions_pending: Whether to open the PR for feat/kilo-plugin now that the extension and the underlying CLI entry points are confirmed working end-to-end.
Whether the 3 pre-existing test failures (asfdk version drift, before_agent_start hook registration in the Pi extension factory) should be triaged/fixed in a follow-up thread.
handoff_record.next_agent_notes: The MCP context server should now work after a plain Zed restart (or even just a context-server reconnect), with no settings.json intervention required, because `asfdk-harness-mcp` is now both on PATH (npm link) and functionally correct (entrypoint.ts fix). If Zed's Extensions panel 'Configure' button wipes the settings.json override again, that is expected/known and harmless now — do not chase it further; verify instead that `printf '<initialize JSON>\n' | asfdk-harness-mcp` responds immediately. If it does not, re-run `npm run build && npm link` from the repo root before re-diagnosing anything Zed-side.
